steps.description: Corporate Secretary determines whether the resolution will be adopted at a duly noticed meeting or by written consent, and initiates the appropriate path.

evidence.quote: Board resolutions may be adopted at a duly noticed meeting or by written consent

steps.description: Corporate Secretary provides written notice to all directors at least 10 days before the meeting date.

evidence.quote: the Corporate Secretary must provide written notice to all directors at least 10 days before the meeting date

steps.description: Board votes at the meeting; a quorum (majority of total directors) must be present for the vote to be valid.

evidence.quote: A quorum, consisting of a majority of the total number of directors, must be present for a meeting vote to be valid

steps.description: For written consent path, all directors must sign the resolution unless the bylaws authorize a lesser threshold.

evidence.quote: Written consent resolutions require the signature of all directors unless the bylaws expressly authorize a lesser threshold

steps.description: General Counsel reviews the resolution before it is recorded in the corporate records.

evidence.quote: The General Counsel must review all resolutions before they are recorded in the corporate records

steps.description: Corporate Secretary records the resolution and files it in the corporate minute book within 5 business days of adoption.

evidence.quote: The Corporate Secretary then records the resolution and files it in the corporate minute book within 5 business days of adoption

steps.description: For stock issuance resolutions, Corporate Secretary files with the Secretary of State within 30 days of adoption.

evidence.quote: Resolutions authorizing the issuance of stock must additionally be filed with the Secretary of State within 30 days of adoption
